chief_complaint: painful clicking and locking of ring finger in flexed position when grasping objects
hpi_details: 53F with diabetes presenting with catching/locking of right ring finger during extension and tender nodule palpable over the A1 pulley at MCP joint.
ideas: She thinks she is developing severe arthritis in her hand or that a tendon in her knuckle slipped out of its groove.
concerns: She is worried that her finger will stay permanently stuck and that she won't be able to type at work or cook for her family.
expectations: She hopes to get a finger splint or a cortisone shot so she does not have to undergo surgery.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Dupuytren's contracture without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

teaching.one_liner: 53F diabetic with painful clicking and locking of her ring finger in flexion with a tender A1 pulley nodule.
red_flags: Fever, spreading redness, marked swelling, or severe pain with passive finger extension requires urgent assessment for hand infection
Diabetes increases risk and may complicate healing

must_ask.say: Does your finger get stuck in a bent position, and do you have to force it straight?
Can you feel a small lump at the base of that finger in your palm?
How well controlled is your diabetes currently?

must_ask.objective: Ask about which activities trigger the catching
must_ask.say: Does this happen more when you grip objects tightly?

must_ask.objective: Explain steroid injection and surgical options
must_ask.say: If examination confirms trigger finger and there are no infection signs, treatment can include activity changes or a steroid injection; with diabetes, we would discuss temporary blood-glucose elevation. Persistent locking may need hand-surgery review.

history.answer: My right ring finger keeps clicking and locking bent whenever I grip something, and it is quite painful.
It is only in my right ring finger, right at the base of the finger in my palm. All my other fingers and my left hand feel completely normal.
It started gradually about three weeks ago with occasional catching, but over the last week it gets stuck bent almost every day.
It is a dull ache at rest, but when the finger catches or pops straight it is a sharp 5 out of 10 pain.
When I make a fist and try to straighten my hand, the ring finger gets stuck in a bent position. I usually have to use my other hand to pop it straight.
Yes, I felt a small, tender bump right at the base of that finger on my palm. It hurts whenever I press directly on it.
It happens whenever I grip things tightly, like carrying grocery bags, turning door handles, or holding the steering wheel.
No, there is no redness, heat, or general swelling along my finger or hand.
The finger feels particularly stiff and stuck bent when I first wake up in the morning, and it takes some time to loosen up.
Gripping tightly or lifting heavy objects makes it catch more often. Resting my hand and running warm water over it seems to ease the tightness.
It makes everyday chores awkward because I try to avoid gripping firmly with my right hand, though I can still manage basic tasks.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, I never injured, bumped, or twisted my finger. The clicking sensation just developed on its own.
No, I have never had catching or locking in any of my fingers before.
No, I have not experienced unusual tiredness, low fevers, or unintended weight loss.
No skin rashes, mouth ulcers, hair loss, eye redness, or dryness in my eyes or mouth.
No, I do not have morning back stiffness, heel pain, or swollen sausage-like fingers or toes.
No recent diarrhea, burning with urination, discharge, or sore throat.
I eat a balanced diet without excessive alcohol or red meat, and I do not take any water pills.
No, I have never had cortisone injections, hand surgery, or artificial joint replacements.
I have been happily married in a monogamous relationship for over twenty years, and there is no concern for any infections.
I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes five years ago and manage it mostly through diet and walking. My last hemoglobin A1c was 6.9 percent two months ago.
I thought maybe I was getting severe arthritis or that a tendon in my knuckle slipped out of place.
I'm really worried my finger will get permanently stuck and I won't be able to type at work or even cook.
I was hoping you could give me a splint or an injection to loosen it up so I don't need surgery.
I have type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and slightly elevated cholesterol.
I had my gallbladder removed ten years ago without any problems, and no other surgeries or hospitalizations.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day in the morning for my blood pressure, and a daily multivitamin.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked or used tobacco products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine at social dinners, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an administrative assistant doing office work and typing, and I live with my husband.
My mother had type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, but no one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis or joint deformities.
My periods stopped two years ago when I went through menopause, so there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/80 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 36.6 °C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-appearing woman in no acute distress, resting her right hand comfortably in her lap.
No erythema, warmth, rash, flexor sheath streaking, or trophic skin changes on either hand.

Tender palpable nodule over the right ring finger A1 pulley at the metacarpophalangeal joint, with painful clicking and locking in flexion during active extension that releases with gentle manual assistance.
Full 5/5 muscle strength in intrinsic and extrinsic hand muscles bilaterally, limited only by mechanical triggering in the right ring finger.
Intact light touch sensation and normal two-point discrimination across median, ulnar, and radial nerve distributions bilaterally.
Radial and ulnar pulses are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally, with capillary refill under two seconds in all digits.
